title: Main Deck Cargo Floor Attachment Provisions for Freighter Conversion, Frames 40 to 54
abstract: Introduction of build-standard hard points and reinforced floor panel edges in the centre fuselage so that a later passenger-to-freighter conversion does not require the floor grid to be opened up.

sections.reason: Conversion houses converting the type to freighter configuration were removing and re-installing the entire main deck floor grid between frames 40 and 54 because the passenger build has no load introduction points where the freighter restraint system needs them. That work accounted for roughly 40 per cent of the conversion downtime and produced a fatigue-critical re-drilled joint that had to be individually substantiated on every aircraft. Two conversion houses and one lessor asked Aeralis to build the provisions in from new so that the conversion becomes a bolt-on rather than a rebuild.
sections.description: Sixteen machined hard points are introduced in the cargo floor panel structure between frames 40 and 54, four per bay, aligned with the freighter restraint grid. The aft cargo floor gusset kit D5350137657469 is replaced by a heavier item carrying the inboard pair of hard points, and the forward cargo floor splice plate sub-assembly ES657922-93 is extended outboard to pick up the outer pair. The upper cargo floor lug sub-assembly HA342629-96 is added at each hard point as the load introduction fitting. Panels are retained with countersunk screws AGS895094-3D at a reduced pitch across the reinforced edges. In passenger configuration the hard points are capped and carry no load; only the mass penalty is present. Work is inside the aircraft in zones 133, 142 and 225 with the cabin floor covering lifted. Revised detail is on drawings D53501330193 and D53501381747.
sections.effects: Mass increase of 63 kg per aircraft in passenger configuration, essentially at the centre of gravity, with no reportable balance effect. No electrical load change. Not interchangeable: a provisioned floor panel set cannot be mixed with the earlier standard in the same bay because the edge fastener pitch differs. Conversion downtime is expected to fall by eighteen to twenty-two days.
sections.embodiment_note: Cut in on the production line at MSN S01705 in September 2022 as a build standard for all twin-engine aircraft. Retrofit for delivered aircraft is offered through Service Bulletin SLN-53-1045 but is only economic when taken together with a conversion; the SB says so explicitly.

type_data.balance_impact: Distributed about the centre of gravity; no reportable shift
type_data.production_impact: Cut-in at MSN S01705; adds 14 hours to the Section 14 floor grid build
